title: Range Sum Queries

concept.title: Answer many range sums with one table
body: If you add up the elements again for every query, many queries on a long array are too slow. Instead build the prefix sums once: `p[i]` is the sum of the first `i` elements, with `p[0] = 0`.

body.code:
p = [0] * (n + 1)
for i in range(n):
    p[i + 1] = p[i] + a[i]
# sum of a[l..r] (1-based, inclusive):
answer = p[r] - p[l - 1]

body: The sum of a block is the prefix up to its end minus the prefix just before its start. After the O(n) preparation, every query costs O(1).

statement: You are given an array of `n` integers and `q` queries. Each query gives two positions `l` and `r` (counting from 1). Print the sum of the elements from position `l` to position `r`, both included.
inputFormat: Each of the next `q` lines has `l` and `r`.
outputFormat: Print `q` lines, one answer per query.
hints: Adding up the block for every query is too slow when n and q are large.
Build `p` where `p[i]` is the sum of the first i elements.

explanation: Build prefix sums once. A block sum is a difference of two prefix sums, so each query takes constant time.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, q = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
qs = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(q)]

p = [0] * (n + 1)
for i in range(n):
    p[i + 1] = p[i] + a[i]
out = []
for l, rr in qs:
    out.append(p[rr] - p[l - 1])
print("\n".join(map(str, out)))
